title: Completed differentials for a supplied finite formal parameter map
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $(B,\mathfrak n)$ a complete Noetherian local $k$-algebra whose coefficient map induces $k\cong B/\mathfrak n$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Let $e\geq0$, let $R=k[[T_1,\ldots,T_e]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and let $\varphi:R\to B$ be a local $k$-algebra map making $B$ a finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Set $b_i=\varphi(T_i)$ and $\widehat\Omega_{B/k}=\varprojlim_m\Omega_{B/k}/\mathfrak n^m\Omega_{B/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Then $\widehat\Omega_{B/k}$ is a finite $B$-module and the following sequence is exact, with the indicated maps:
$$B^e\xrightarrow{(c_i)\mapsto\sum_i c_i\,\mathrm db_i}\widehat\Omega_{B/k}\longrightarrow\Omega_{B/R}\longrightarrow0.$$
The last map is induced by the universal derivations, and $\Omega_{B/R}$ is finite and complete for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology.

source.place: Expose IV 1.2.5 (completed differentials) and 2.1.12, exact sequence displayed across pp. 52–53 and the identification of completed with ordinary relative differentials for finite A/A_0.

proof.text: Write $M=\Omega_{B/k}$, $\widehat M=\varprojlim_m M/\mathfrak n^mM$, and $\iota:M\to\widehat M$ for the canonical map. Choose generators $x_1,\ldots,x_s$ of $\mathfrak n$, which exist by Noetherianity. For any derivation $\delta:B\to V$ and $q\geq1$, expanding a product of $q$ elements of $\mathfrak n$ by the Leibniz rule gives $\delta(\mathfrak n^q)\subseteq\mathfrak n^{q-1}V$; coefficients cause no difficulty, since their differential terms lie in $\mathfrak n^qV$. For $b\in B$ choose $a\in k$ with $b-a\in\mathfrak n$, write $b-a=\sum_j u_jx_j$, and choose $a_j\in k$ lifting the residues of $u_j$. Thus $b-a-\sum_j a_jx_j\in\mathfrak n^2$ and $\mathrm db\equiv\sum_j a_j\mathrm dx_j\pmod{\mathfrak nM}$. Since the symbols $\mathrm db$ generate $M$, the classes of $\mathrm dx_j$ generate $M/\mathfrak nM$ over $B/\mathfrak n=k$.

source.place: Definition 07BK (definition-differentials) and Lemma 00RO (lemma-universal-omega); elementary calculation using the given residue-field section

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] with $A=B$, $I=\mathfrak n$ and the arbitrary module $M$. The ideal is finitely generated by Step 1, so $\widehat M$ is separated and complete and its first projection identifies $\widehat M/\mathfrak n\widehat M$ with $M/\mathfrak nM$, carrying $\iota(\mathrm dx_j)$ to $\mathrm dx_j$. The ring $B$ is $\mathfrak n$-adically complete by hypothesis. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-ring], including its clause about any chosen lifts of generators, says that the $\iota(\mathrm dx_j)$ generate $\widehat M$ over $B$. In particular $\widehat M$ is finite and $\iota$ is surjective: every sum $\sum_j c_j\iota(\mathrm dx_j)$ is $\iota(\sum_j c_j\mathrm dx_j)$.

Put $E=\Omega_{B/R}$ and choose finite $R$-module generators $y_1,\ldots,y_t$ of $B$. For every $b=\sum_j\varphi(r_j)y_j$, the $R$-derivation satisfies $\mathrm d_{B/R}b=\sum_j\varphi(r_j)\mathrm d_{B/R}y_j$. Since universal differential symbols generate $E$, these finitely many differentials generate $E$ as a $B$-module. The hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-complete-over-complete-noetherian] hold with ring $B$, ideal $\mathfrak n$ and module $E$: $B$ is Noetherian and complete and $E$ has just been shown finite. Hence the canonical map $c_E:E\to\varprojlim_m E/\mathfrak n^mE$ is bijective. This proves both asserted properties of the ordinary relative differential module.

source.place: Definition 07BK (definition-differentials), Lemma 00RO (lemma-universal-omega), and Tag 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor), part (3); compare ILO IV 2.1.12, p. 52

proof.text: The derivation $\mathrm d_{B/R}$ is a $k$-derivation because $\varphi$ is a $k$-algebra map. The universal property gives $v:M\to E$, $\mathrm d_{B/k}b\mapsto\mathrm d_{B/R}b$. Its $B$-linearity gives maps $v_m:M/\mathfrak n^mM\to E/\mathfrak n^mE$ commuting with all quotient transitions. Define $q=c_E^{-1}\circ\varprojlim_m v_m:\widehat M\to E$. Then $q\iota=v$, since both maps have the same reduction in every $E/\mathfrak n^mE$. The symbols $\mathrm d_{B/R}b$ generate $E$, so $q$ is surjective. Also $q(\iota(\mathrm d_{B/k}b_i))=0$, since $b_i=\varphi(T_i)$. Let $L\subseteq\widehat M$ be the $B$-span of these $e$ vectors and $Q=\widehat M/L$, with quotient map $\pi$. The images in $Q$ of the finite generating family in Step 2 generate $Q$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-complete-over-complete-noetherian] to this finite $B$-module: $Q$ is complete and separated. The map $q$ descends to $\bar q:Q\to E$.

source.place: Definition 07BK (definition-differentials), Lemma 00RO (lemma-universal-omega), and Tag 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor), part (3); explicit construction of the right arrow in ILO IV 2.1.12

proof.text: Set $\delta=\pi\iota\mathrm d_{B/k}:B\to Q$, a $k$-derivation with $\delta(b_i)=0$. For $f=\sum_\alpha c_\alpha T^\alpha\in R$ and $m\geq1$, let $P_m=\sum_{|\alpha|\leq m}c_\alpha T^\alpha$. The tail $f-P_m$ belongs to $(T_1,\ldots,T_e)^{m+1}$: group each tail monomial by one of the finitely many monomial divisors of total degree $m+1$, leaving a formal series as its coefficient. Localness of $\varphi$ gives $b_i\in\mathfrak n$, whence $\varphi(f-P_m)\in\mathfrak n^{m+1}$. On the polynomial $P_m$, additivity and Leibniz give $\delta(\varphi(P_m))=0$. The estimate proved in Step 1 therefore gives $\delta(\varphi(f))\in\mathfrak n^mQ$ for every $m\geq1$. Separatedness of $Q$ from Step 4 implies $\delta(\varphi(f))=0$. Thus $\delta$ is an $R$-derivation. For $e=0$ every $f$ is already constant and this argument has zero tail.

source.place: Expose IV 1.2.5 (continuous derivations), p. 49, and IV 2.1.12, pp. 52-53; elementary truncation argument identifying the cokernel

proof.text: The universal property of $E=\Omega_{B/R}$ now gives $h:E\to Q$ with $h(\mathrm d_{B/R}b)=\delta(b)$. For every $b\in B$ we have $\bar qh(\mathrm d_{B/R}b)=\mathrm d_{B/R}b$, so $\bar qh=\mathrm{id}_E$. Conversely $h\bar q(\pi\iota(\mathrm d_{B/k}b))=\pi\iota(\mathrm d_{B/k}b)$. These vectors generate $Q$: the symbols generate $M$, and $\iota$ and $\pi$ are surjective by Steps 2 and 4. Therefore $h\bar q=\mathrm{id}_Q$. We have proved that $\bar q$ is an isomorphism, so $\ker q=L$. The image of $B^e\to\widehat M$, $(c_i)\mapsto\sum_i c_i\iota(\mathrm d_{B/k}b_i)$, is exactly $L$. This proves the displayed exact sequence with the specified maps; its right map is the actual completion of the map of universal differentials constructed in Step 4.

Steps 3-4: the 00MA node applies with ring B, ideal n to the finite modules E and Q. Step 5: the tail lies in (T)^{m+1}, φ is local so its image is in n^{m+1}, the Leibniz estimate from Step 1 and separatedness of Q make δ an R-derivation.
